findings.title: Kubernetes bearer token can be sent over plaintext HTTP
findings.where: scripts/lib/kube-client.mjs:40-43 accepts PROBAITIO_KUBE_API verbatim; scripts/lib/kube-client.mjs:73-81 attaches the bearer token and fetches that URL.
findings.what: The client documentation requires an HTTPS Kubernetes endpoint, but resolve() performs no scheme validation. Setting PROBAITIO_KUBE_API to an http:// URL causes call() to place PROBAITIO_KUBE_TOKEN in an Authorization header sent without TLS, exposing a cluster credential to network interception.
findings.fix: Parse the configured API URL once in resolve(), reject non-https: schemes, credentials, and malformed URLs, then return the normalized HTTPS origin. Keep the in-cluster URL construction unchanged.
findings.acceptance: A focused test configures PROBAITIO_KUBE_API=http://127.0.0.1:<listener-port> with a sentinel token, invokes call(), and verifies rejection occurs before any request reaches the listener; an equivalent https:// configuration remains accepted.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial second pass re-read the configuration and fetch path at baseline c8b98a29508b5eb7725c75a7e2a41dfa94c1feba. No intervening URL parser or protocol guard exists: the environment string is only stripped of trailing slashes before fetch receives the bearer-authenticated request.
